newsitem.title: POLAND: SWARZEDZ SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE NEW ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: SWARZEDZ SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE NEW ISSUE.

text.p: Swarzedz SA shareholders approved an issue of up to 6.625 million shares, with 3.125 million in a debt-for-equity scheme and 3.5 million in a one-for-one rights issue to current shareholders, the Polish furniture maker said.

"The decision on the new share issue opens the way to an agreement on financial restructuring with the main creditors of Swarzedz SA," it said in a statement after an extraordinary shareholders meeting unanimously voted for the management plan.
"The restructuring will concern indebtedness of the Swarzedz SA capital group towards financial institutions (and therefore not suppliers) of 60.5 million zlotys," it said.
Swarzedz said its main creditor banks had approved the restructuring scheme and agreement should be sealed in weeks, while the issue itself was expected in the second half of 1997.

The company said the issue to creditors would settle a major part of its debts, while the rest would be paid in coming years out of increased sales which would result from investing proceeds from the rights issue.
It aimed to boost 1997 production and sales to 170.9 million zlotys this year, 60 percent above sales last year.
Overdue payments to suppliers would be paid off gradually, after negotiations with individual companies, it added.
Swarzedz made a net loss of 38.9 million zlotys last year.
Its main creditors are Polish Development Bank SA (PBR), Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA, Bank Gdanski and Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
